items.note: The whole reason to come, and it changes every month — there is no fixed dish to order. Vegetables come mainly from the Yazaki farm in Ikoma, the noodle broth and the miso are made in-house, and the cooking follows shokuyojo, the idea of eating to keep the body in balance. One April set was fuki-butterbur mixed sushi, new onion and chicken with crisp bonito flakes, mugwort-fu dengaku, new-potato miso soup and pickles; a summer one was pork yanagawa-style with a soft-cooked egg, mozuku vinegar, colourful namul, nori tsukudani, rice, a lotus-seed soup and syrup-preserved winter melon. Soy, dashi and miso run through everything.
A larger seasonal variant of the monthly set.
The lighter option if you do not want the full teishoku.
For when you want a drink rather than a meal.

Changes every two months and is deliberately small — sized so you can still eat it after the set meal — with real spice and herb aromatics and restrained sweetness. Reported at ¥1,000–¥1,300 depending on the build. Recorded versions: chestnut and rum raisin (white chestnut cream, vanilla ice, granola, rum-raisin ice, dark coffee jelly); hojicha and citrus; Earl Grey and baked apple; caramel nuts and baked apple; strawberry-mascarpone mille-feuille. Granola and mille-feuille both mean wheat.

The owner's own blend, and heavier on spice than most: cinnamon, kola nut, vanilla, clove, lemongrass and cardamom, each roasted first to bring the aroma up. Sold as a glass, or as a ¥1,000 bottle of syrup to take home.

items.ja: 自家製ソーダ（しそ・梅・ジンジャー・レモン）
items.en: House sodas — shiso, plum, ginger, lemon
items.note: Made from house syrups; you can float ice cream on top to make it a soda float.

Brewed through a cloth filter rather than paper, which lets more of the oils through and gives a rounder cup. This was the coffee programme of the neighbouring inn Kohaku, moved into the shokudo; the cafe side still trades under the name Kissa Kohaku.

items.ja: 国産和牛のすき焼き（宿泊者向け）
items.en: Domestic wagyu sukiyaki (for guests at the inn)
items.note: Not served in the shokudo — this is at Kohaku, the owner's guesthouse a minute north, added to the room rate, minimum two people, book ahead. It revives the tradition of Hiyoshikan, the old Nara inn where art and history students gathered and sukiyaki was the house dish. Sukiyaki's warishita sauce is soy, sugar and mirin.

items.ja: 自家製スモーク盛合せ
items.note: The dish to start with. Four kinds: house prosciutto of Baak pork, smoked Piyotama egg, smoked oyster and smoked scallop. Price is per person. Note there is no paper menu here — you read it on a screen but order out loud.

items.ja: ホタルイカと菜の花の和ヒージョ
items.note: The shop's pun: ajillo made Japanese ('wa'). Firefly squid are the tiny bioluminescent squid caught in Toyama Bay in spring; available February to May only.

items.ja: ヤングコーンのカダイフ風フリット
items.en: Baby corn fried in its own silk, kadaif-style
items.note: The corn silk is wound around the cob and fried so it crisps like kadaif pastry — a neat trick. Served with a white-miso aioli. Batter is wheat and aioli contains egg.

items.ja: 鰻肝の赤ワイン煮、香草パン粉仕上げ
items.romaji: unagi-kimo no aka-wain ni, kousou panko shiage
items.en: Eel liver in red wine under herb crumb
items.note: The escargot-in-herb-butter technique applied to eel liver — the clearest statement of what this kitchen does, French method on Japanese ingredients. Panko is wheat.

Chicken-and-beef bouillon set as a jelly, house umeboshi paste, and — the local touch — hand-stretched noodles from Miwa Yamamoto. Miwa in Nara is the birthplace of somen, hand-stretched wheat noodle, made there since at least the 8th century. Topped with Baak pork prosciutto.

items.ja: ヤマトポークの洋風ルーロー天津飯
items.romaji: Yamato Pooku no youfuu ruuroo tenshinhan
items.en: Yamato Pork lu rou fan under a crab-style omelette
items.note: Taiwanese braised pork given French spicing, then capped with egg the way a tenshin-han is. Yamato Pork is Nara's branded pig. Soy sauce throughout.

items.ja: 大和牛の挽き肉カレー
items.note: Took second place in the 2010 black-rice curry competition. Two grinds of beef are used — one fine to build the sauce, one coarse for texture — against vegetable sweetness and tomato acidity. From the shop's earlier premises; ask whether curry is still served. Japanese curry base is a wheat roux.

items.ja: 大和肉鶏手羽先の薬膳カレー
items.en: Medicinal curry with Yamato chicken wings
items.note: Yamato-nikudori is Nara's slow-grown branded chicken, firmer and more flavourful than commodity birds. Yakuzen means the spicing follows Chinese medicinal principles.

items.ja: 季節野菜のベジタリアンカレー
items.note: Explicitly vegetarian on the shop's own listing, which is rare here — but confirm the stock and whether the roux contains dairy. From the earlier premises.
Local sake lengthened with soda; the sake changes daily — Mimurosugi junmai ginjo karakuchi on one visit.
From Toyosawa Brewery in Nara city.

items.ja: 奈良の地酒（純米・純米吟醸・純米大吟醸・燗酒）
items.note: A deep Nara list at roughly ¥700–¥800 a glass — including Harushika from Imanishi Seibei in Nara city, and its 'Nara no Yaezakura', brewed with yeast isolated from cherry petals in a collaboration with Nara Women's University. Nara-grown Hinohikari table rice is used in some of them.
Brewed in Koryo, Nara prefecture. Beer is barley.
There is a ¥500 per-person seat charge — worth knowing before the bill arrives.

Weekdays to 1pm. Caesar-dressed risotto-style leaf salad, your pick of seven spaghetti or two risottos, a small house gelato and a drink. Recent reports put the walk-in lunch nearer ¥1,000–¥1,500. Note the shop is a pasta specialist — it says plainly that it serves nothing but pasta unless you pre-order.

Weekdays 11:30–12:30 only, last order 12:30, and it sells out — after that you go on to the ordinary pasta lunch. Worth phoning or messaging ahead; they take same-day bookings until noon and there is a ¥1,100 no-show charge.

items.ja: 生パスタ（タリアテッレ／リングイネ／パッパルデッレ）
items.en: Fresh pasta — tagliatelle, linguine or pappardelle
items.note: The shop's obsession, and you choose the shape: tagliatelle is an egg noodle cut flat like kishimen, linguine is pressed oval and springy with a faint sweetness, pappardelle is wide and soft. Upgrading a dish to fresh pasta costs about ¥100. Fresh egg pasta means wheat and egg.

items.ja: ガーリックと鷹の爪のピリ辛オイルソース
items.romaji: gaarikku to takanotsume no pirikara oiru soosu
items.en: Garlic and chilli oil spaghetti (aglio e olio)
items.note: The simplest on the list. A tomato version is the same price.

items.ja: 自家製トマトソースとモッツァレラチーズ
items.romaji: jikasei tomato soosu to mottsarera chiizu
items.note: The shop names the fresh tomato and mozzarella pairing as its own favourite.

items.ja: ベーコンときのこのクリームソース
items.romaji: beekon to kinoko no kuriimu soosu
items.note: The same pairing is offered in tomato, tomato-cream and bonito-dashi soy versions, all ¥1,320.

items.ja: ベーコンときのこの鰹だし醤油
items.romaji: beekon to kinoko no katsuo-dashi shouyu
items.en: Bacon and mushroom in bonito-dashi soy
items.note: The wafu (Japanese-style) pasta that Japan invented and Italy never asked for — bonito stock and soy instead of a Mediterranean sauce, and lighter than most cream pastas. Soy sauce is wheat.

items.ja: ベビーホタテのクリームソース
items.note: Also in tomato and tomato-cream at ¥1,320, and with mushroom in dashi-soy at ¥1,300.

items.ja: 黒オリーブとアンチョビのトマトソース
items.romaji: kuro oriibu to anchobi no tomato soosu

items.ja: 自家製スモークチキンのクリームソース
items.romaji: jikasei sumooku chikin no kuriimu soosu
items.note: A spicy tomato version is the same price. The smoking is done in-house.

items.ja: 自家製スモークサーモンのクリームソース
items.romaji: jikasei sumooku saamon no kuriimu soosu
items.note: Cherry-smoked in-house; also appears in the summer course.

items.ja: 海老のトマトクリームソース
items.note: A prawn-and-scallop tomato is the same price.
Add ¥100 to have it on fresh pasta. Pesto contains cheese.
The shop calls it its number-one pizza; house tomato sauce and cheese. Allow about 20 minutes. Note the current site says pizza must be arranged the day before.

items.ja: チーズとブラックペッパー（20cm）
items.en: Cheese and black pepper pizza, no tomato
items.note: Described by the shop as snack-like.

items.ja: 黒オリーブ・ケッパー・アンチョビ（20cm）
items.en: Black olive, caper and anchovy pizza
Meat dish for two or three
items.note: From ¥1,800. Must be arranged by the day before — the shop is a pasta specialist and does not keep these on hand.

items.en: Fish dish for two or three
items.note: From ¥1,700, day-before order.

Order two days ahead. The July–August 2026 run: prosciutto and tomato marinated salad; fresh pasta with prawn and olive tomato; cherry-smoked salmon in basil cream; wagyu tagliata with marsala and balsamic and potato gnocchi; house gelato and cheesecake; coffee or tea. ¥3,200 before tax.
Made in the restaurant; a small scoop comes with the lunch set. Strawberry has been on.

items.ja: きたまちチーズケーキ
items.note: Named for the Kitamachi district the restaurant sits in; a regulars' favourite.
The house signature. Dorayaki is two small pancakes around sweet red bean; here they are cooked only after you order, so it arrives hot rather than wrapped. Wheat batter and egg.

Rice-flour dumplings grilled on a skewer and glazed with a sweet soy syrup — also made to order, so they come off the grill hot. The dumplings themselves are rice, but the mitarashi glaze is soy sauce, which is wheat.

items.ja: 大和茶の抹茶・煎茶・ほうじ茶
items.en: Yamato tea — matcha, sencha and hojicha
items.note: The point of the shop, which opened in spring 2026 as the group's first tea-led room: Nara-grown Yamato-cha, from the highlands east of the city where tea has been cultivated since the 9th century. Served in Akahada-yaki, the local Nara pottery, painted with Nara motifs.

From ¥600. The parent company is a specialty roaster that also wholesales green beans; the water is spring water from the Yoshino district. Hot coffee and lattes come in Akahada-yaki bowls, hot tea in French cups. You smell the options and pick.
Chosen by sniffing the leaf before you commit — the shop hands you the aromas to taste-test.
Spring only. Cherry syrup with a salt-preserved cherry blossom opening on the surface as it warms. Contains dairy.

From ¥300. The group's own loaf, made with Nara-grown wheat and organically farmed ingredients, and named after Mount Mikasa behind Kasuga Shrine. It was created deliberately against the sweet 'luxury shokupan' fashion — hard-looking crust, soft chewy crumb, no sweetness. Wheat.

From ¥2,500. Built on Yamato-yasai heirloom vegetables, Yamato beef, Yamato pork and Yamato chicken from local farms and roadside producers. The group's sandwiches, sausages and hams are supplied to a well-known hotel restaurant.
A proper non-alcoholic list, which is unusual in Nara.
Opening hours are extended on Friday and Saturday evenings for wine. Wine is often animal-fined.

items.en: Kama-nuki udon — noodles straight from the pot
items.note: This is what the shop is for, and it is worth understanding. Normally boiled udon is rinsed in cold water to firm the surface and wash off starch. Kama-nuki skips that: the noodles are lifted straight out of the cauldron and served, so the surface stays soft, starchy and fragrant and the chew is looser than you expect. The dough is hand-kneaded and every strand hand-cut at a board facing the street. Udon is wheat, entirely — nothing here is gluten-free.

items.en: Kake udon — noodles in hot broth
items.note: The plain bowl and the honest test of the noodle. Hot dashi broth over the noodles, nothing else. The broth is bonito-and-kombu dashi with soy, so neither vegan nor gluten-free.
Beef simmered in a sweet-salty soy braise, laid over the noodles. Wagyu options are on the menu, which is unusual at this price bracket.
The shop's headline bowl: beef braised to order in a sweet-salty sauce, tangled with a runny onsen egg so the yolk coats the noodles. Also served cold.
Sesame and chilli in the Sichuan manner, on udon rather than Chinese noodles.

items.en: Kitsune udon — with sweet fried tofu
items.note: A sheet of aburaage simmered in sugar and soy until it is sweet and dripping. Named after the fox, said to love fried tofu — and this is the Kansai form of the dish, where kitsune always means udon.

items.ja: ハイカラうどん（天かす）
items.note: Not a menu line so much as a move: tenkasu, the crisp scraps of fried tempura batter, sit on the counter for you to add yourself, and a bowl of kake plus tenkasu is what Kansai calls haikara udon. The crumbs soften into the broth and enrich it.
Fried to order, not held. One plate held prawn, shishito pepper, aubergine and chicken. Eaten with the table salt or the dashi-soy on the counter rather than dipped in the udon broth.
Tempura is also sold piece by piece — prawn, chicken and aubergine among them.
Chicken in tempura batter rather than karaage dredge — softer, lighter.
Wheat batter and a shared fryer.
Curry broth thickened with starch so it clings to the noodles. Listed in the shop's category tags; ask whether it is on that day.
